newsitem.title: USA: Chigaco Fed Moskow says monetary policy lags.
newsitem.headline: Chigaco Fed Moskow says monetary policy lags.

text.p: Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Michael Moskow said Wednesday that lags in monetary policy may make anticipation necessary.
When asked about the idea of a pre-emptive credit tightening to ward off inflation, Moskow said "I think that monetary policy has long lags.

"What we're trying to do is look ahead, going forward, and what we're trying to maintain is steady, stable growth -- maximum sustainable growth," he said, speaking to reporters after a speaking engagement near here.
"I think at some point you're going to have to anticipate in your actions."

Moskow said that inflation risks were on the high side and that at this point in the business cycle, "we are very vigilant ... in looking to see whether there are any incipient pressures building up."
Moskow declined to comment on questions about the high level of U.S. stocks or on recent comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

U.S. markets have been closely watching various comments from the Fed chief regarding whether U.S. stocks' rise is sustainable. Last week Greenspan had suggested the Fed may be willing to raise short-term interest rates to ward off inflation risks.
